findings.finding: Double-trap detection uses mstatus.SDT for HS-mode traps, but the spec requires checking sstatus.SDT (the effective S-mode SDT) when in HS-mode. The code reads io.in.mstatus.SDT directly. Since sstatus is an alias of mstatus for the SDT field, this works functionally, but the intent is unclear and fragile — if the alias implementation diverges, double-trap detection breaks.
findings.snippet:
private val m_EX_DT  = handleTrapUnderM  && mstatus.MDT.asBool  && hasTrap
private val s_EX_DT  = handleTrapUnderHS && mstatus.SDT.asBool  && hasTrap
private val vs_EX_DT = handleTrapUnderVS && vsstatus.SDT.asBool && hasTrap

findings.finding: When MDT is written to 1, MIE is cleared — correct per Smdbltrp spec. However, if MDT was already 1, writing MDT=1 again (a redundant write) also clears MIE. The condition 'when (w.wdataFields.MDT && w.wen)' should check that the write actually changes MDT from 0 to 1, not any write that sets MDT=1. A redundant MDT=1 write could clear MIE through a CSR access that isn't intended to change the trap-disable state.

writeSDT computation at line 578 uses a Mux that, when DTE=0 and writing via alias sstatus, passes reg.SDT.asBool (the current value) as writeSstatusSDT. This means if reg.SDT is already 1 (from a prior mstatus write when DTE=1) and DTE is subsequently cleared to 0, an sstatus write would compute writeSDT = true despite DTE=0. The guard at line 583 prevents reg.SDT from actually changing, but the writeSDT signal at line 587-589 would still clear SIE. This means: writing sstatus when DTE=0 and SDT was previously 1 causes SIE to be spuriously cleared.

LCOFIP update logic has a priority issue. The when-elsewhen chain checks fromSip/fromVSip/wen first, then lcofiReq, then keeps the old value. If lcofiReq fires in the same cycle as fromSip/wen, the lcofiReq edge is lost because fromSip/wen takes priority. The spec requires that the hardware LCOFI interrupt be captured in mip.LCOFIP independent of software writes.

MEnvCfg extends EnvCfg which declares STCE, PBMTE, ADUE, DTE as RO(0) by default (CSRBundles.scala:69-72). Only when CSRConfig.EXT_SSTC/EXT_DBLTRP are true are these fields promoted to RW. If EXT_DBLTRP is compiled as false but hardware actually has the double-trap logic, DTE would be RO 0 — software can never enable it. Conversely, if EXT_SSTC is true, STCE resets to 1, meaning supervisor timer interrupts go through stimecmp by default on boot.
MRET correctly forces V=Off when MPP=M, preventing virtualization under M-mode. When MPP is U/S, V inherits from mstatus.MPV. Matches RISC-V privileged spec section 3.1.6.1.
findings.snippet:
outPrivState.PRVM := in.mstatus.MPP
outPrivState.V    := Mux(in.mstatus.MPP === PrivMode.M, VirtMode.Off.asUInt, in.mstatus.MPV.asUInt)

findings.finding: Trap entry to M-mode correctly sets: privState = ModeM, mstatus.MIE=0 (interrupts disabled in handler), mstatus.MPIE=old MIE, mstatus.MDT=1 (double-trap armed), mepc=trapping PC, mcause=transformed cause (double-trap detection replaces cause with EX_DT). mtval2 captures original precause on double-trap. Fully spec-compliant.
findings.snippet:
out.privState.bits            := PrivState.ModeM
out.mstatus.bits.MIE          := 0.U
out.mstatus.bits.MDT          := 1.U
out.mcause.bits.ExceptionCode := Mux(isDTExcp, ExceptionNO.EX_DT.U, highPrioTrapNO)
out.mtval2.bits.ALL           := Mux(isDTExcp, precause, tval2 >> 2)

findings.finding: trapPCGPA is taken directly from input (line 48) with no width limit: 'val trapPCGPA = in.trapPcGPA'. Different page-table levels produce GPAs of different bit widths (Sv39x4 has 41-bit GPA, Sv48x4 has 50-bit GPA). If in.trapPcGPA carries stale high bits beyond the actual GPA width, it leaks into mtval2 for guest page faults, causing information leakage cross-VM through the mcause/mtval pair visible to M-mode.

Mideleg correctly implements: (a) M-level interrupts (MSI, MTI, MEI) are RO 0 — never delegatable past M-mode. (b) VS-level interrupts (VSSI, VSTI, VSEI) are RO 1 — always delegated past M-mode to HS when H extension is present. (c) SGEI is RO 1 — mandatory delegation to HS. (d) Local interrupts are RO 0 — cannot be delegated. (e) LCOFI is RW — selectively delegatable per AIA spec. All reset to 0 where writable.

Medeleg correctly marks MCALL (ecall from M-mode) and DBLTRP (double trap exception) as read-only 0 — these exception codes are never delegatable past M-mode. All other exceptions are RW and reset to 0 (not delegated).

mstatus.MDT resets to mdtInit which is 0 (CSRConfig.scala:71). The Smdbltrp spec does not mandate a specific reset value, but MDT=0 at boot means M-mode starts without double-trap protection. Any exception in early boot (before software sets MDT=1) cannot be detected as a double trap, violating the security safety net the extension is designed to provide. The comment 'as current test not support clean mdt' confirms this is a workaround, not an intentional design.

mnstatus.NMIE resets to 1 and is fully writable — code to make 'write 0 have no effect' is commented out. Per Smrnmi spec, NMIE should be HW-writable (set by HW on NMI entry, cleared by HW on NMI exit) and SW writing 0 should have no effect. The current implementation allows software to clear NMIE=0, which per-spec is only allowed via mnret. This means software can disable NMI handling at will, potentially masking hardware NMIs.

MRET correctly: (a) sets MPP=U (lower privilege), (b) sets MPV=Off, (c) restores MIE=MPIE, (d) sets MPIE=1, (e) clears MPRV when returning to non-M mode, (f) clears MDT when returning from M-mode handler, (g) clears SDT when returning to mode below M and HS. vsstatus.SDT is correctly handled for VU-mode returns. Matches privileged spec.
findings.snippet:
out.mstatus.bits.MDT    := 0.U
out.mstatus.bits.SDT    := Mux(mretToM || mretToS, in.mstatus.SDT.asBool, 0.U)
out.vsstatus.bits.SDT   := Mux(mretToVu, 0.U, in.vsstatus.SDT.asBool)

findings.finding: rwStimecmp_EX_II logic at line 225 reads: '!privState.isModeM && (!mcounterenTM || !menvcfgSTCE) && (addr === CSRs.vstimecmp.U || addr === CSRs.stimecmp.U)'. Per Sstc spec, when menvcfg.STCE=1, stimecmp/vstimecmp ARE accessible from S/VS mode (assuming mcounteren.TM=1). This condition traps when EITHER mcounteren.TM=0 OR menvcfg.STCE=0. But when STCE=1 and TM=0, the spec says stimecmp is still accessible — the trap should only fire when STCE=0 (extension disabled). The '||' should be '&&' between the negations: '!mcounterenTM && !menvcfgSTCE'.
findings.snippet: private val rwStimecmp_EX_II = !privState.isModeM && (!mcounterenTM || !menvcfgSTCE) && (addr === CSRs.vstimecmp.U || addr === CSRs.stimecmp.U)

findings.finding: csrIsRO at line 208 checks addr(11,10)==='b11'.U to detect read-only CSRs. Per privileged spec, CSR addresses with addr[11:10]=11 are read-only ONLY in the standard address ranges. Custom CSR ranges can override this. For addresses in custom ranges (0xBC0-0xBFF, etc.), addr[11:10]=11 could be a writable custom CSR, but this code would incorrectly trap writes to it as illegal.
findings.snippet:
private val csrIsRO = addr(11, 10) === "b11".U
private val rwIllegal = csrIsRO && wen

findings.finding: mip.STIP correctly becomes read-only when menvcfg.STCE=1, driven by platformIRP.STIP (hardware timer). Writes to STIP via CSR instruction or mvip alias are blocked when STCE=1. The reg.STIP register hold path in 'otherwise' silently preserves state rather than trapping, which is correct WARL behavior for writes to RO fields.
